topPRs.title: fix(core): ground connector response routing in authorized action names
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Direct connector requests could be treated as retrieved instructions, and the first response decision had no evidence of which actions were available. Real Discord-shaped requests sometimes replied that two registered tools were unavailable without calling them. This change distinguishes the current sender's request from reference material and supplies a complete permission-checked action-name index before routing.

- The inbound envelope preserves user-priority requests while quotes, forwards, attachments, platform references and tool output remain data. Runtime identity, roles, approvals and tool authorization remain authoritative; sender metadata cannot select envelope purpose. The default reference wrapper and complete content are preserved.
- Direct text decisions and context-read continuations receive sorted authorized action names. Existing private, role, connector and validation gates run on each composition. Descriptions and schemas remain in planner discovery, including when the name index is longer than a tiny full catalog. No additional model call or domain-provider refill is introduced.
- Regression coverage exercises actual initial/recomposed model requests, one/360-action catalogs, private/role denial, changed validation and stable ordering. The existing wrapper-routing test retains its no-action contract with the current warning.

Closes #31745.

Source qualification at `22ce841d089a516a29feb32164a6bf77c9dbd1e0`:
- Pinned install, 635 tests across 11 core/security files, core typecheck and lint pass. Full root `bun run verify` passed in 726.70 seconds.

topPRs.title: fix: retain interpretation context and defer planning providers
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Stage 1 could reply without authorized cross-room history, pending choices or bot-loop evidence while receiving unrelated provider context. This change admits the evidence needed to interpret a message, defers domain inventories and widget grammar to planning/completion, and keeps context ownership consistent through caching, recovery and restoration.

- Explicit provider selections cannot be broadened by hooks or cached planner state. The selection participates in cache and concurrent-composition identity.
- Cross-room fallback is suppressed only when the dedicated provider actually participates. Identity/disclosure gates remain intact; failures are unavailable states rather than empty successful history. Standalone MEMORY_SEARCH children remain discoverable.
- Planning/completion have an explicit phase independent of tool presence. Opted-in widget hosts advertise only routing in Stage 1 and compose requested controls later; pending acknowledgments cannot finish the turn. Default host widget registration is unchanged.
- Progressive discovery uses the authorized catalog independently of the routed slice. Wrong or unresolved action hints cannot hide other permitted families; an empty denied catalog does not trigger implicit discovery.
- Direct-human IGNORE decisions can receive one model review after context reads and earlier repairs. Contradictory STOP/IGNORE plus pending-work declarations receive bounded reconciliation and fail before effects if still contradictory. Valid silence and stop decisions remain available.
- Context reads retain the complete previous decision as untrusted model output, preserving pending-work reasoning without treating routing descriptions as tool availability. Same-response context-restoration reads union their valid scopes and reauthorize once; malformed batches and later repeated restoration reject without effects.

No stored history, tool receipt or original model input is summarized or truncated. Existing persona compaction and the Personal-crisis rule removal on develop are preserved. Connector-envelope wording is handled separately under #31745.

Closes #31734.

Validation:
- Source revision `1ce5a3abc89c44c7d5788dba6d5df79404f8cfc2`: pinned install; 778 core tests in 20 files; 86 agent tests in 7 files; three real adapter schema-wire tests; 26 prompt tests; secret checks; and complete root `bun run verify` passed (923.79 seconds).

topPRs.title: fix(finances): classify bill dueness on the owner's calendar day
topPRs.author: hermesagent270-commits
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Fixes #31062 — `FinancesService.getUpcomingBills` compared bare `YYYY-MM-DD` due dates against the UTC calendar day, so a bill due today became `overdue` at 16:00 in Los Angeles and a bill due yesterday stayed `upcoming` until 09:00 in Tokyo. Supersedes the approach closed in #31064 per the maintainer review there: one time zone owner, the same resolved zone on both advertised surfaces, absent configuration distinguished from failed resolution, both entry points exercised.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop`
      with zero conflicts (`git fetch origin && git rebase origin/develop`).
- [x] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync, or any failure is
      recorded below with the exact unrelated blocker.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the
      evidence attached below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased/merged onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts (`1eba34ba95`).
- [x] `bun run verify` passes post-sync: 373/373 workspace tasks and all repository audits, exit 0 at `5a18df43` with the pinned Bun 1.3.14 / Node 24.15.0 install (8m55s turbo phase, uncached).

# Risks

Low to medium; the change is confined to how "today" is derived for bill dueness.

- New `packages/shared/src/lifeops-normalize/calendar-time-zone.ts` is the single owner: `registerCalendarTimeZoneResolver(runtime, resolver)` stores one owner-zone resolver on the runtime (a global-symbol property, so a dist and a source copy of the module see the same registration), `resolveCalendarTimeZone(runtime, now)` resolves owner zone → agent `TIMEZONE` setting → host zone and reports the `source`, and `calendarDateKey(now, timeZone)` produces the owner-day key.
- Fail-closed: a resolver that throws is a `LifeOpsServiceError` 503 `CALENDAR_TIME_ZONE_UNAVAILABLE` (cause preserved); an invalid zone from the owner or the setting is 422 `CALENDAR_TIME_ZONE_INVALID`. No step falls through to another zone. A `null` owner zone is "not configured" and continues to the setting; that is the only fallthrough.
- `FinancesService.getUpcomingBills` derives `todayIso` from `calendarDateKey(now, (await this.resolveCalendarTimeZone(now)).timeZone)`; the wrapper rethrows the shared error as `FinancesServiceError` with the same status and code, which `runPaymentsHandler` already turns into `success:false` and `runFinancesRoute` into `ctx.error(res, message, status)`. The action constructs `new FinancesService(runtime)` and the route `new FinancesService(runtime, {ownerEntityId})` exactly as before; neither needs injection because the owner lives on the runtime.
- The personal-assistant plugin registers `resolveConfiguredOwnerTimeZone` in `init`, next to the other first-turn registries. It reads the owner facts through `ownerFactsToView`, so the active-travel destination override is honoured like every other owner-zone consumer, and it propagates a store read failure instead of substituting the host zone (the lenient `resolveOwnerTimeZone` used by reminders is unchanged).
- Behavioral change for operators: an invalid owner or `TIMEZONE` zone now surfaces as an error on the bills route and the dashboard action instead of a silently UTC-classified list. Documented in `plugins/plugin-finances/README.md`.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Moves calendar time zone ownership into `@elizaos/shared`, registers the personal-assistant owner facts as that owner, and makes the finances bill classification read the owner's calendar day from it on every surface.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking; additive exports).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes require a change to the project documentation, and it is included in this PR (`plugins/plugin-finances/README.md`, `TIMEZONE` row).

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

- `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/routes/finances-calendar-time-zone.pglite.integration.test.ts` — real runtime (normally registered personal-assistant plugin, finances schema on PGlite, real runtime-plugin HTTP dispatcher). One bill due `2026-03-02`, `now = 2026-03-03T03:30Z`. Owner fact `America/Los_Angeles` → `upcoming` through both `runPaymentsHandler` (`dashboard`) and `GET /api/lifeops/money/bills`; owner fact `Asia/Tokyo` → `overdue` on both; owner fact `Mars/Phobos` → action `success:false` with `{status: 422, code: CALENDAR_TIME_ZONE_INVALID}` and the route 422 naming the zone. It also asserts the resolver registered by `init` resolves with `source: "owner"`.
- `plugins/plugin-finances/src/upcoming-bills-calendar-time-zone.test.ts` — stubbed repository; owner-zone, setting, host-default, precedence, 503 on resolver failure with cause, 422 on invalid owner or setting zone.
- `packages/shared/src/lifeops-normalize/calendar-time-zone.test.ts` — the owner's precedence and fail-closed contract and the LA/Honolulu/Tokyo/UTC date-key table.

## Detailed testing steps

```bash
bun run --cwd packages/shared test
bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-finances test
cd plugins/plugin-personal-assistant && bunx vitest run --config vitest.src-integration.config.ts src/routes/finances-calendar-time-zone.pglite.integration.test.ts
```

Results at `5a18df43`:

| Lane | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/shared` full suite | 232 files, 2907 tests passed |
| `plugins/plugin-finances` full suite | 16 files, 206 tests passed |
| personal-assistant `src-integration` lane, the new dual-surface test | 4/4 passed on a real PGlite runtime |
| personal-assistant owner fact-store and plugin-init tests | 7 files, 65 tests passed |
| `typecheck` in `packages/shared` and `plugins/plugin-finances` | exit 0 |
| Biome on every touched file | clean |

Red on develop is the reproduction table in #31062 (real runtime, owner fact `America/Los_Angeles` and `TIMEZONE=Pacific/Honolulu` both `overdue` at `2026-03-03T03:30Z` for a `2026-03-02` bill); the new integration test asserts the opposite classification through both surfaces at this head.

# Evidence Gate

sets this marker from the live PR head; rerun it after every push.

topPRs.title: fix(plugin-form): honor registered control types and preserve calendar dates
topPRs.author: hermesagent270-commits
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Fixes #31049. The branch targets `develop` at `886df6eba0c33e40da1794f5e632da6c094bedea`.

# Background and change

`FormService.registerControlType` owned a per-runtime registry, but top-level validation, parsing, formatting, and both extraction prompts consulted only the separate legacy `registerTypeHandler` map. A registered custom type therefore did not govern a top-level field; the built-in date parser also serialized host-local midnight as a UTC instant and could shift a stated day.

The service now passes its registered `ControlType` to top-level validation and display. The evaluator, single-field extractor, and correction detector resolve the same type at their model/parse boundaries; standalone helpers take an additive, explicit type or resolver argument so one agent's custom registry cannot bleed into another's. An explicit legacy `TypeHandler` still overrides a built-in, while a per-runtime custom `ControlType` wins over that global legacy handler. Date-only answers normalize to a validated `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar day; explicit-year ISO, numeric, and English month-name formats are supported, while yearless or impossible dates remain invalid for re-asking. Sensitive display masking still precedes a type's formatter.

# Risks and documentation

Moderate compatibility risk at the date boundary. Unsupported time-bearing, yearless, and locale-ambiguous input is now invalid rather than silently changed into a plausible saved date. Existing persisted timestamp-shaped values have no reliable original calendar-day provenance; this PR does not invent a migration or silently reinterpret them. Owners should assess those legacy sessions before release. No UI or route was changed. The plugin's existing README registration contract is implemented without a new global registry.

# Testing

- Clean `origin/develop` baseline: three exact-source probes fail for Tokyo date normalization (`2026-09-14T15:00:00.000Z` instead of `2026-09-15`), registered custom validation (healthy fallback), and the missing model-facing extraction hint. The same three probes pass at this head.
